candidates.title: Perplexity-Spectrum Calibration for Post-Training Pruning of Large Language Models
candidates.venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
candidates.abstract: Post-training pruning enables efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) without costly retraining, but it relies on calibration data for weight importance estimation. Related studies analyze the impact of calibration data along two dimensions: data sources and input formats. However, once the dataset is fixed, calibration samples are typically selected by random sampling. Therefore, sample selection within the same data source remains underexplored. We propose a perplexity-spectrum calibration sample selection strategy. This strategy uses the target model’s perplexity to measure sample difficulty. It sorts the candidate pool by perplexity and selects a contiguous difficulty window as the calibration set. We evaluate this strategy on three 7B models: Qwen2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Llama-2-7B. Both Wanda and SparseGPT are tested under 2:4 sparsity. Experiments show that the medium-difficulty window centered at the median achieves the best pruning results across all settings. Compared to random sampling, this strategy reduces perplexity degradation by 20%–26% on WikiText-2. On four zero-shot downstream reasoning tasks, it reduces the standard deviation by 3.4–6.1×. Further analysis reveals that medium-difficulty samples induce stronger and more selective neuron activations. This improves pruning mask consistency (Jaccard similarity) from 0.74 to 0.82. The strategy requires one forward pass to score the candidate pool and a sorting step. It serves as an efficient, plug-and-play calibration optimization step.

candidates.title: Share-Manipulation Weight Leakage in 2PC Transformer Inference
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Turing Award Celebration Conference - China 2026
candidates.abstract: We study outsourced 2PC Transformer inference in which a malicious client colludes with one computation party and manipulates unauthenticated intermediate shares. Under protocols with layer-by-layer evaluation, plaintext logit output, and piecewise-linear activations, internal shares become chosen state-oracles that leak exact, projected, or directional weight information. On a compact Transformer the attack recovers the classifier to relative error 1e-8, obtains column-projected output and value matrices, extracts second-FFN effective responses with row cosine 0.986, and recovers first-FFN directions with column cosine 0.994. Query and key projections and embedding matrices remain unrecoverd due to special structure of attention blocks, which are not yet addressed by current attack approaches. The result is partial weight leakage but still a significant threat to model privacy.
candidates.reason: 要旨は外部委託された2者計算Transformer推論で未認証の中間シェアを悪性クライアントが操作し、層ごと評価と平文ロジットをオラクル化して重みを復元する攻撃を実証しており、安全なTransformer推論プロトコル設計への直接の技術的知見である。

candidates.title: PCA: Persistence-Aware Compression and Aggregation for Fast Video Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
candidates.abstract: Despite advances in Video Large Language Models (VLLMs) that have displayed promising outcomes in video understanding, the redundancy in the long-duration frames remains a hindrance to efficient reasoning. This paper introduces a training-free Persistence-Aware Compression and Aggregation (PCA) method designed to preserve high-fidelity raw visual information before the encoding stage. PCA can be built on arbitrary VLLMs and consists of two modules: 1) A Dynamic Downsampling (DD) module that adaptively removes redundant frames by analyzing frame-wise similarity. 2) A Persistence-Aware Motion Enhancement (PAME) module that enriches each selected keyframe by aggregating the temporal context of its neighbors, ensuring that essential information is preserved even after aggressive frame reduction. Our approach substantially reduces the computation of long-context modeling, while enhancing the performance of the baseline model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PCA consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in both efficiency and accuracy, achieving a speedup of 1.8× to 2.5× compared to the baseline VLLM. The code is open-sourced at Heisenberg10110/PCA.
candidates.reason: 要旨は動画LLM向けにフレーム類似度で冗長フレームを動的ダウンサンプリングし近傍の時間文脈をキー フレームへ集約する学習不要のPCAで長尺動画の計算量を削減しており、VLLM推論の前処理圧縮として直接の効率化貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: DConstrain: Compiling Context-Parameterized Transitions for Diffusion Language Model Constrained Decoding
candidates.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) decode multiple tokens in parallel, so individually valid tokens can be incompatible together under a schema. Exact joint inference over a grammar graph enforces compatibility, but it requires token-labeled successors across many hypothetical parser configurations. Encoding stacks and field histories in compiled states can cause exponential growth, which forces prior exact decoders to fix property orders and exclude valid outputs. We present DConstrain, which compiles schemas into context-parameterized transition programs. Cold compilation specializes token consumption to local grammar states while retaining context-dependent stack operations, environment guards, and caller-dependent deferred parsing symbolically. Tracking field histories as runtime values supports arbitrary property order without enumerating field subsets offline. At runtime, warm compilation binds reached configurations to these programs to construct exact successors, overlapping with the model forward pass because graph construction requires no model scores. Furthermore, token-effect grouping merges tokens with identical compiled effects before runtime contexts are bound, so groups are reused across stacks and environments even when concrete successors differ. Objective-specific score aggregation and token restoration provably preserve both the Viterbi optimum and the token-labeled path distribution of ungrouped inference. Across three benchmarks and two DLM families, DConstrain compiles 100% of BFCL schemas under arbitrary property orders, whereas an optimized finite-state baseline compiles only 71.30-85.81%. Under arbitrary property order, it reduces BFCL end-to-end decoding latency by 6.65-46.26 times with 100% schema validity and raises DiffusionGemma's BFCL accuracy from 37.27% under fixed order to 81.56%.

candidates.title: An Efficient Transformer with Distance-aware Attention
candidates.venue: 2023 IEEE 9th Intl Conference on Big Data Security on Cloud (BigDataSecurity), IEEE Intl Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing, (HPSC) and IEEE Intl Conference on Intelligent Data and Security (IDS)
candidates.abstract: In recent years, the transformer model has become one of the main highlights of advances in natural language processing (NLP). The attention mechanism of the transformer model makes it possible to track the relations between words across very long text sequences in both forward and reverse directions. However, the complexity of the attention mechanism is quadratic and introduces a performance bottleneck in the transformer. We propose a distance-aware attention mechanism which integrates the locality information by assigning different weights to query-key pairs according to the distance between the query and the key. By doing so, we in fact shrink the dimension of the matrix in the vector matrix multiplication and reduce the complexity of the attention to O(n2/m). Experiments show that the distance-aware attention is superior to or close to the original model and other variants in various NLP tasks.
candidates.reason: 要旨はクエリ・キー間距離に応じて重み付けしベクトル行列積の次元を縮小して注意計算量をO(n2/m)へ下げる距離対応注意を提案し実験で示しており、Transformer注意機構の計算効率化という推論にも直結する直接貢献が確認できる。
